character.centerRule: Joseph son of Jacob remains distinct from every same-name person; his descendants and tribal uses stay marked as later memory rather than being narrated as Joseph’s own actions.

phases.orientation: Joseph is born into Jacob’s household, marked by Rachel, paternal favor, brothers, reports, a tunic, and dreams.

phases.orientation: A journey to his brothers becomes stripping, confinement, sale, false evidence, and transport into Egypt.

phases.orientation: Judah’s appeal is followed by disclosure, weeping, invitation, reunion, and the settlement of Jacob’s household.

phases.orientation: Jacob’s final requests and blessings lead into burial, renewed fear, Joseph’s reply, an oath about bones, and Joseph’s death.

phases.orientation: Joseph’s body, descendants, tribal name, land, and story are carried through law, poetry, prophecy, wisdom, retelling, and apostolic memory.

character.throughline: Joseph remains the human center as family favor, dreams, sale, enslavement, refusal, accusation, confinement, interpretation, authority, testing, disclosure, famine policy, blessing, death, bones, descendants, and later memory gather around him.

passages.excerpt: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
passages.observation: At thirty Joseph travels through Egypt and stores produce until the grain can no longer be counted.
passages.title: Joseph gathers grain through the years of abundance

dimensions.label: Joseph attributes forgetting and fruitfulness to God
Toil, his father’s house, and affliction remain inside the names

passages.excerpt: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
passages.observation: Joseph and Asenath’s two sons receive names through which Joseph speaks about toil, his father’s house, and fruitfulness in affliction.
passages.title: Manasseh and Ephraim are named before the famine

dimensions.label: Joseph opens the storehouses and sells grain
Severe famine sends many lands to Joseph

passages.excerpt: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
passages.observation: The seven abundant years end; famine widens, storehouses open, and Pharaoh directs Egypt’s cry for bread toward Joseph.
passages.title: The famine begins and people are sent to Joseph

dimensions.label: Ten brothers descend to buy grain
Fear for Benjamin recalls the loss of Joseph

passages.excerpt: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
passages.observation: Jacob sends ten sons toward Egypt but withholds Benjamin because he fears harm to Joseph’s full brother.
passages.title: Ten brothers descend for grain while Benjamin remains

dimensions.label: Joseph recognizes them while remaining unrecognized

passages.excerpt: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
passages.observation: Joseph recognizes the brothers, remembers his dreams, speaks as a stranger, charges them as spies, and confines them together.
passages.title: The brothers bow before an unrecognized governor

dimensions.label: Joseph revises the test, overhears the brothers, weeps, and binds Simeon
The brothers recall Joseph’s distress at the pit

passages.excerpt: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
passages.observation: Joseph offers a path to life, hears the brothers connect distress to their treatment of him, turns aside to weep, and binds Simeon.
passages.title: “I fear God” frames a test involving Benjamin

dimensions.label: A lodging place on the road
Joseph restores the money and supplies food for the journey
The brothers ask what God has done to them

passages.excerpt: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.
passages.observation: Joseph commands provisions and restored money; the discovery in one sack turns the brothers’ attention toward what God has done.
passages.title: Grain, returned money, and fear on the road

dimensions.label: The brothers report the governor’s demand
Jacob names Joseph and Simeon as lost

passages.excerpt: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these thing…
passages.observation: The brothers recount the governor’s demand, discover every bundle of money, and meet Jacob’s claim that Joseph and Simeon are gone.
passages.title: Jacob hears the report and refuses Benjamin

dimensions.label: Jacob prepares gifts and sends the sons
Gift, double money, and grain sacks
Jacob entrusts the brothers to God Almighty

passages.excerpt: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
passages.observation: Renewed hunger forces the unresolved demand into view; Judah pledges himself and Israel entrusts the sons to God Almighty.
passages.title: Judah guarantees Benjamin before the second descent

dimensions.label: The steward prepares the household meal and restores Simeon
The steward attributes the returned treasure to their God

passages.excerpt: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine…
passages.observation: Benjamin’s presence changes Joseph’s instructions; the brothers explain the money while the steward speaks of peace and their God.
passages.title: Fear at Joseph’s house meets the steward’s reassurance

dimensions.label: Joseph questions, blesses Benjamin, weeps privately, and orders the meal
Recognition and affection remain hidden behind separate tables

passages.excerpt: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
passages.observation: Bowing, questions about Jacob, blessing over Benjamin, private tears, separate tables, rank, and Benjamin’s fivefold portion shape the feast.
passages.title: Joseph sees Benjamin, weeps privately, and orders the meal

dimensions.label: The cup is planted, sought, and found
All the brothers return to the city

passages.excerpt: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have y…
passages.observation: Joseph’s command places the cup with Benjamin; accusation, denial, search, torn clothes, and return follow.
passages.title: A silver cup turns the brothers back toward the city

dimensions.label: The others are offered peace only by leaving Benjamin behind

passages.excerpt: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”
passages.observation: Joseph names the discovered deed and limits enslavement to Benjamin, while the others are told they may return in peace.
passages.title: Judah and his brothers fall before Joseph again

dimensions.label: Judah retells the family history and offers himself
The lost brother and Jacob’s grief
Benjamin’s return is placed against Judah’s freedom

passages.excerpt: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
passages.observation: Judah retells the family’s loss and the father’s attachment, then asks to remain as slave so Benjamin can return.
passages.title: Judah offers himself in Benjamin’s place

dimensions.label: Joseph clears the room, weeps, discloses himself, and embraces his brothers
Joseph says God sent him ahead to preserve life
The brothers’ sale and God’s sending are both named

passages.excerpt: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
passages.observation: Joseph clears the room, weeps, identifies himself, draws the terrified brothers near, and speaks of God sending him ahead to preserve life.
passages.title: Joseph makes himself known and names preservation

dimensions.label: Pharaoh invites the household and Joseph equips the brothers
Joseph warns the brothers not to quarrel on the way

passages.excerpt: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
passages.observation: Pharaoh welcomes the family; Joseph supplies wagons, clothing, money, provisions, and a final warning not to quarrel on the way.
passages.title: Pharaoh and Joseph equip the brothers for return

dimensions.label: The brothers report Joseph alive and show the wagons
Jacob’s spirit revives and he resolves to travel

passages.excerpt: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
passages.observation: The report first leaves Jacob numb; Joseph’s words and wagons revive his spirit and turn him toward a final meeting.
passages.title: Jacob hears that Joseph lives and rules in Egypt

dimensions.label: Israel sacrifices and the household begins the descent
God promises presence, nationhood, return, and Joseph’s hand at Jacob’s eyes

passages.excerpt: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
passages.observation: At Beersheba God addresses Israel’s fear, promises a great nation and return, and places Joseph at Jacob’s deathbed.
passages.title: God promises to descend with Jacob and names Joseph’s hand

dimensions.label: The household is counted by family lines
The household total will be stated differently in Acts 7

passages.excerpt: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
passages.observation: The family group distinguishes those who descend from those already born in Egypt and closes with the household total.
passages.title: Joseph, his sons, and the household are counted

dimensions.label: Joseph meets Jacob and prepares the household’s answer to Pharaoh
Father and son are reunited in Egypt

passages.excerpt: Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
passages.observation: Judah leads the way, Joseph arrives by chariot, the father and son meet, and Joseph prepares the family’s occupation for Pharaoh.
passages.title: Joseph meets Jacob in Goshen and weeps on his neck

dimensions.label: Joseph presents his family, settles them, and supplies bread
Jacob’s household receives a possession in Egypt

passages.excerpt: Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had comman…
passages.observation: Joseph presents brothers and father to Pharaoh, receives Goshen, places the household in Rameses, and provides bread by family size.
passages.title: Joseph settles and provides for the household

dimensions.label: The people of Egypt and Canaan
Joseph gathers money and then exchanges bread for livestock
Livestock replaces exhausted money as payment

passages.excerpt: They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he…
passages.observation: Severe famine exhausts money in Egypt and Canaan; Joseph gathers payment for Pharaoh and then supplies food in exchange for livestock.
passages.title: Money and livestock are exchanged for bread

dimensions.label: Joseph buys land, relocates people, distributes seed, and establishes a fifth
Pharaoh gains the land while priestly land remains excepted

passages.excerpt: Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.
passages.observation: The Egyptians offer themselves and their land; Joseph buys the land for Pharaoh, relocates the people, supplies seed, and establishes the fifth.
passages.title: Land, seed, and a fifth become Egypt’s arrangement

dimensions.label: The burial place of Jacob’s fathers
Jacob asks for loyal burial and Joseph swears

passages.excerpt: but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place.” Joseph said, “I will do as you have said.”
passages.observation: As Jacob’s death approaches, he asks Joseph for loyal action, receives an oath, and bows at the bed’s head.
passages.title: Jacob binds Joseph to burial outside Egypt

dimensions.label: Jacob recalls God Almighty’s promise of fruitfulness and land
Rachel’s death remains inside the family account

passages.excerpt: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
passages.observation: Joseph brings Manasseh and Ephraim to his sick father; Jacob recalls God’s promise and claims the two sons within his own tribal household.
passages.title: Jacob recalls Luz and adopts Joseph’s sons

dimensions.label: Joseph presents his sons and Jacob crosses his hands
Joseph objects while Jacob says he knows
Jacob invokes the God who shepherded and redeemed him

passages.excerpt: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to M…
passages.observation: Joseph presents his sons in birth order, Jacob crosses his hands, Joseph objects, and Jacob knowingly places Ephraim ahead while blessing both.
passages.title: Jacob crosses his hands over Ephraim and Manasseh

dimensions.label: Jacob names the Mighty One, Shepherd, Stone, and God of Joseph
Joseph is described as separated from his brothers

passages.excerpt: The blessings of your father have prevailed above the blessings of my ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient hills. They will be on the head of Joseph, on…
passages.observation: Vine, archers, strength, shepherd, stone, divine help, abundance, and separation from brothers converge in Jacob’s words over Joseph.
passages.title: Jacob blesses Joseph as fruitful, attacked, and sustained

dimensions.label: Joseph mourns, embalms, seeks permission, and buries Jacob
The burial party returns to Egypt

passages.excerpt: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
passages.observation: Joseph’s grief leads to physicians, Egyptian mourning, Pharaoh’s permission, a large procession, lament, burial at Machpelah, and return.
passages.title: Joseph mourns, embalms, and buries Jacob

dimensions.label: The brothers send a plea and bow; Joseph weeps and promises care
Joseph refuses God’s place and names God’s intention for good
Human evil and divine preservation are both stated

passages.excerpt: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?
passages.observation: The brothers send a message and bow; Joseph weeps, refuses God’s place, distinguishes intended evil from intended good, and promises provision.
passages.title: The brothers fear repayment after Jacob’s death

dimensions.label: The land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Joseph binds an oath about his bones and dies
Joseph says God will surely visit Israel

passages.excerpt: Joseph took an oath from the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”
passages.observation: Joseph sees later generations, announces his death and God’s coming visitation, requires his bones to be carried, and is placed in a coffin in Egypt.
passages.title: Joseph speaks of visitation, binds an oath, and dies

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Exodus 1:1–8

dimensions.label: Israel multiplies and a new king arises
The king does not know Joseph
Joseph’s death becomes the boundary before oppression

passages.excerpt: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who didn’t know Joseph.
passages.observation: Joseph’s prior presence and death stand behind a multiplying people and a new royal memory gap.
passages.title: A king arises who does not know Joseph

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Exodus 13:17–22

dimensions.label: Etham at the edge of the wilderness
The way of the Red Sea
Joseph’s oath is recalled at departure

passages.excerpt: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had made the children of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones away fr…
passages.observation: The departure route, Joseph’s oath, his bones, divine guidance, cloud, and fire move together at the opening of the wilderness journey.
passages.title: Moses carries Joseph’s bones out of Egypt

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Deuteronomy 33:13–17

dimensions.label: Favor is sought from the one who lived in the bush
Joseph’s name now embraces two tribal multitudes

passages.excerpt: for the precious things of the earth and its fullness, the good will of him who lived in the bush. Let this come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head o…
passages.observation: Dew, deep, sun, moon, ancient hills, the bush, firstborn strength, and the peoples of Ephraim and Manasseh gather around Joseph’s name.
passages.title: Moses blesses Joseph’s land and strength

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Joshua 24:29–33

dimensions.label: The parcel becomes an inheritance for Joseph’s children

passages.excerpt: They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Ham…
passages.observation: After Joshua’s death the carried bones reach land Jacob purchased, becoming an inheritance for Joseph’s children.
passages.title: Joseph’s bones are buried at Shechem

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · 1 Chronicles 5:1–2

dimensions.label: The genealogy distinguishes firstborn, birthright, and rule
The birthright is assigned to Joseph’s sons
Genealogical order does not follow the birthright

passages.excerpt: For Judah prevailed above his brothers, and from him came the prince; but the birthright was Joseph’s)—
passages.observation: The genealogy distinguishes firstborn status, birthright, and Judah’s princely line.
passages.title: Reuben’s birthright is said to pass to Joseph’s sons

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Psalms 78:65–72

dimensions.label: God rejects Joseph’s tent and chooses Judah, Zion, and David
Joseph’s tribal name marks a rejected center
Joseph and Judah are placed on opposite sides of the choice

passages.excerpt: Moreover he rejected the tent of Joseph, and didn’t choose the tribe of Ephraim,
passages.observation: The closing movement moves from divine awakening and enemy defeat to rejected Ephraim, chosen Judah, Zion, and David.
passages.title: The poem contrasts Joseph’s tent with Judah’s choice

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Psalms 80:1–7

dimensions.label: The congregation asks God to shine and restore
God is addressed as Israel’s shepherd who leads Joseph
Joseph’s name describes a flock and a northern tribal grouping

passages.excerpt: Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.
passages.observation: The prayer speaks Joseph as a flock, names Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, and repeatedly asks God to restore and shine.
passages.title: Israel’s shepherd is addressed as one who leads Joseph

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Psalms 105:16–23

dimensions.label: A king and ruler of peoples
Joseph is sent, afflicted, tested, released, and appointed
The LORD calls famine and sends a man ahead

passages.excerpt: He sent a man before them. Joseph was sold for a slave.
passages.observation: Famine, Joseph’s sale, fetters, testing, release, instruction, and Israel’s descent are arranged as remembered preparation.
passages.title: The psalm recalls a man sent ahead through slavery

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Ezekiel 37:15–28

dimensions.label: Two sticks are joined and the divided people are gathered
God promises gathering, cleansing, covenant, and sanctuary
Joseph and Judah move from divided houses to one nation

passages.excerpt: tell them, ‘The Lord GOD says: “Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions; and I will put…
passages.observation: The prophetic sign names Joseph in Ephraim’s hand, joins divided peoples, and follows union with land, king, covenant, and sanctuary.
passages.title: Joseph’s stick is joined with Judah’s stick

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Amos 5:1–17

dimensions.label: The prophet calls for seeking good and establishing justice
The LORD may be gracious to Joseph’s remnant
Religious centers and claims of divine presence stand beside injustice

passages.excerpt: Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts. It may be that the LORD, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
passages.observation: Lament, seeking the LORD, rejecting evil, establishing justice, and possible grace gather around Joseph’s remnant.
passages.title: The remnant of Joseph is addressed amid lament and justice

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Amos 6:1–7

dimensions.label: Leaders feast, make music, drink, and anoint themselves
The first in ease become the first taken captive
Joseph names the afflicted people for whom they do not grieve

passages.excerpt: who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best oils, but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.
passages.observation: Ease, music, wine, oils, and the ungrieved ruin of Joseph precede the announcement of exile.
passages.title: Comfortable leaders are not grieved for Joseph’s affliction

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Wisdom 10:13–14

dimensions.label: A righteous man is sold, confined, vindicated, and raised to authority
Joseph is recalled without his personal name
The retelling attributes continuous action to wisdom

passages.excerpt: When a righteous man was sold, wisdom didn’t forsake him, but she delivered him from sin. She went down with him into a dungeon,
passages.observation: The retelling follows a righteous man through sale, dungeon, bonds, royal authority, false accusation, and enduring glory while making wisdom the continuing actor.
passages.title: Wisdom retells the sold righteous man without naming Joseph

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Sirach 49:13–16

dimensions.label: The writer praises Joseph as leader and supporter
Leadership and remembered remains summarize Joseph

passages.excerpt: Nor was there a man born like Joseph, a leader of his kindred, a supporter of the people. Even his bones were cared for.
passages.observation: A brief ancestral remembrance sets Joseph beside other exceptional figures and explicitly recalls care for his bones.
passages.title: Joseph is praised as leader and supporter

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · 1 Maccabees 2:49–64

dimensions.label: Joseph keeps the commandment and becomes lord of Egypt
Joseph is used as an exhortative ancestral example

passages.excerpt: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and became lord of Egypt.
passages.observation: Mattathias’s final address places Joseph’s commandment-keeping and Egyptian authority within a sequence of ancestral examples.
passages.title: Joseph is recalled among examples under pressure

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · 4 Maccabees 2:1–6

dimensions.label: Joseph’s refusal becomes an example in an argument about reason
The later discourse selects restraint rather than narrating the whole episode

passages.excerpt: on this ground, therefore, the temperate Joseph is praised in that by reasoning, he subdued, on reflection, the indulgence of the senses.
passages.observation: The discourse names Joseph’s response to sexual desire while arguing about reason’s governance of bodily impulses.
passages.title: Joseph’s restraint becomes an example of reasoning

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · 4 Maccabees 18:10–19

dimensions.label: A parent reads ancestral accounts to form the children
Joseph in prison is one remembered example among several

passages.excerpt: He used to read to you about the slaying of Abel by Cain, the offering up of Isaac, and the imprisonment of Joseph.
passages.observation: A remembered parent reads Abel, Isaac, Joseph, Phinehas, and other ancestral accounts while forming the sons’ endurance.
passages.title: A father’s readings included Joseph’s imprisonment

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · John 4:1–6

dimensions.label: Joseph’s land remains part of the setting

passages.excerpt: So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
passages.observation: The Samaritan setting locates Jacob’s well and the parcel associated with Joseph before the conversation at the well begins.
passages.title: Jesus sits near land Jacob gave Joseph

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Acts 7:9–16

dimensions.label: Joseph is sold, rescued, recognized, and joined by his family
God is with Joseph and rescues him
Household number and burial details differ from other Scripture accounts

passages.excerpt: “The patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt. God was with him
passages.observation: The speech moves from the patriarchs’ jealousy through God’s presence with Joseph, elevation in Egypt, famine, recognition, migration, death, and burial.
passages.title: Stephen retells jealousy, sale, presence, and rescue

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Acts 7:17–19

dimensions.label: The people multiply and the king acts craftily against them
Infants are exposed under the new rule

passages.excerpt: until there arose a different king who didn’t know Joseph.
passages.observation: Stephen’s speech turns from multiplying promise to a ruler whose lack of Joseph-memory frames oppression.
passages.title: A different king who did not know Joseph appears

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Hebrews 11:20–22

dimensions.label: Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons and Joseph mentions the departure
The departure and bone instruction are characterized as faith

passages.excerpt: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave instructions about his bones.
passages.observation: The sequence joins Isaac’s blessing, Jacob’s blessing of Joseph’s sons, and Joseph’s final instructions about the exodus and his remains.
passages.title: Joseph speaks by faith about departure and bones

passages.contextLine: Bones, descendants, and later memory · Revelation 7:4–8

dimensions.label: Twelve thousand are sealed from each named tribe
Joseph appears as a tribal name in the list
Joseph and Manasseh are named while Ephraim is not

passages.excerpt: of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, of the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, and of the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.
passages.observation: The enumerated tribes include Joseph beside Zebulun and Benjamin within the numbered sealing vision.
passages.title: Joseph’s tribal name appears among the sealed
